author: AstraSynthesis
reviewer_verdict: Not decision-ready on the reviewed snapshot.
status: Author-repaired and published by Main as an open full non-draft process-4 ballot; owner decision pending. No correction re-review.

beginner.scope: Simulated rli5 of raw ballot, not rendered or human study.
beginner.author_response: Added compiler/proof/model definitions, explicit stage boundaries, and missing-proof predictions. Later challenge repairs were not independently beginner-re-reviewed.

findings.subject: Theorem-to-implementation binding
findings.action: Defined extracted/in-logic, direct-source, and per-result-checker binding shapes. Receipts require the proved object, relation, implementation/checker/certificate identity, and trusted build chain. Abstract algorithm proof plus unrelated Rust implementation is excluded. Concrete major binding architecture remains a later owner choice.

findings.subject: Foreign code-generator suffixes
findings.action: Named per-mode theorem endpoints and trusted rustc/LLVM/linker, Cranelift, and browser tools. A is not an end-to-end physical-machine theorem. Absence of a Rust/Cranelift model is limited to the collected corpus; no literature-wide impossibility claim is adopted.

findings.subject: Prelude and compile-time scope
findings.action: Full A includes compile-time evaluation and Jet-owned Prelude/runtime implementations against their contracts, not only marshalled calls. Partial options explicitly identify which reachable operations are covered. Rust verification/model prerequisites remain missing, not silently assumed solved.

findings.subject: Preservation relation and finite resources
findings.disposition: Accepted and repaired without weakening I9.
findings.action: Defined target refinement, allowed traces, configuration/scheduling/resource premises, and promised progress. Target-only exhaustion is allowed only under ratified semantics and failed declared premises. Otherwise it requires a separate owner semantic decision. No generic timeout or undefined-behavior carve-out.

findings.subject: Conditional success, checker rejection, and proof-cell consistency
findings.action: Acceptance/coverage remain separate gates because preservation can hold for an always-rejecting compiler. Rejected/unknown checking takes a deterministic proved fallback or fails internally; performance gates still apply. Required proof cells cannot be filled by tests.

findings.subject: Credible partial-proof alternatives
findings.action: Added back-half proof, reference-interpreter proof, and executable-formal-model options. Kept source-processing and existing-evidence options. Every losing option has an explicit why-not. A remains the recommendation, with shared foreign-tool exposure stated fairly.

findings.subject: Design-away and genuine losses
findings.action: Replaced no-guaranteed-date with an unmeasured proof obligation gating 1.0 and renewed correspondence after covered semantic changes. Recorded cost, checker, reuse, and scope attempts for every option. Historical proof sizes are context, not a reason to reject the better outcome.

findings.subject: Advertised-denominator escape
findings.action: Fixed the denominator to ratified I9 modes and applicable capabilities. Dropping a mode or capability requires a separate owner decision and any necessary carve-out.

findings.subject: Same-workload surface evidence
findings.action: Current surface shows a documented library workflow, explicitly not run here, and distinguishes program evidence from a compiler theorem. In-the-wild uses CompCert library compilation. Dirty-tree build failure remains research/card context, not the policy rationale.

findings.subject: Formal model authority
findings.action: The model is trusted and validated against ratified law, I5 examples, and conformance. Repair model mistakes; unresolved semantic changes require owner decision. Proof is not application intent.

findings.subject: CompCert parser and bootstrap precision
findings.action: Current CompCert comparison names its proved parser plus Clight-to-assembly phase and real external boundaries. CakeML in-logic bootstrap is distinguished from ordinary out-of-logic self-hosting. Existing #217 evaluation remains, with no port approval.

findings.subject: Why proof matters when tests remain
findings.action: Added the historically scoped Csmith result and explicit independent roles for tests: model validity, acceptance/coverage, unproved components, integration, and external assumptions.

findings.subject: Padded gains and review provenance
findings.action: Removed independent tests as an A-only gain because all options retain them. Recorded exact author/adversarial families and fresh-agent provenance. Review metadata was mechanically shortened for Tower without claiming any additional review.

scope_limits: One Fable challenge only; no correction re-review, generic report review, or new research review.
Source/evidence comparisons do not establish current compiler execution.
Author repairs are substantive judgments, not a claim that Fable approved the repaired draft.

The owner permits Astra-model authorship/publication from Main or AstraSynthesis, not Luna. Main published and read back the final ballot by serialized coordination. Astra's earlier rejected add attempts created no ballot.
